name: turbopuffer
tagline: Serverless vector and full-text search on object storage, priced for billions of documents.
description: turbopuffer is a proprietary serverless search engine that stores every namespace on object storage and caches hot data on NVMe and in memory, so cold data costs object-storage prices while warm queries stay fast. It provides vector (ANN), BM25 full-text and hybrid search with attribute filtering, strongly consistent reads by default and namespaces suited to one-per-tenant designs. It became popular with AI companies that index huge numbers of small corpora, such as code-editor and workspace products. Expect higher cold-query latency than RAM-resident engines and plan minimums from $16 per month.

pricing.notes: Usage billed on storage (~$0.33/GB), data written and data queried. Plans: Launch $16, Scale $256, Enterprise $4,096 monthly minimums; Enterprise adds BYOC, CMEK and single tenancy.

scale.notes: Namespaces on object storage scale to very large document counts; customers run millions of namespaces.

strengths: Object-storage-first design makes large, mostly-cold datasets cheap
Vector, BM25 and hybrid search with filters in one API
Namespaces scale to millions of tenants
No clusters to size or operate
weaknesses: Closed source, cloud-only (BYOC only on Enterprise)
Cold namespace queries are noticeably slower than warm ones
Narrower query features than a full search engine
useCases: Per-user or per-repo indexes for AI coding and productivity tools
notIdealFor: Consistently ultra-low-latency queries on cold data
